verdict.rationale: Capacities' first-party docs describe block references and embeds. You type `((` to link to an individual block, you can embed blocks and their children in another page, and an embedded block is identical to the original, so edits appear everywhere it is used. That covers referencing, transclusion and live sync. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that embedded blocks stay in sync in practice.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can reference or transclude an individual block or section of one note inside another and have it stay in sync

citations.quote: Capacities lets you link to individual blocks inside of an object, and reference them in other pages. We call this concept block-based linking or just block references.
it also lets you embed individual blocks and their children inside another page.
An embedded block is identical to the original. This means that any edits will occur in all places where this block is used.
Type `((` anywhere in your content and a search will open. Search for the content of the block you want to link to.
